title: At 95 and battling Alzheimer's, Tony Bennett sang every word of "Fly Me to the Moon" with Lady Gaga
desc:
Even when memory fades, music has a way of finding its way back in.
Researchers at Northwestern Medicine say familiar music is processed in several areas of the brain, including regions that can remain relatively preserved in people living with Alzheimer's and dementia. That's why songs can sometimes help patients reconnect to emotions, memories, and even lyrics.

Before his passing, Tony Bennett and Lady Gaga shared years of friendship, performances, collaboration, and deep admiration for one another. In this moment, when Gaga asked him to sing
"Fly Me To The Moon," he remembered every word.

title: Tony Bennett Remembered Lady Gaga One Last Time — Their Final Song Together 🎤💞
desc:
When Tony Bennett began losing his memory to Alzheimer’s, one thing never faded — the music.
And beside him through it all was Lady Gaga. 💔

“He saved my life, now I’m trying to save his,” she once said.

At his final concert, she whispered,

“You ready, Tony?”
He smiled:
“I’m always ready when you are, Lady Gaga.”

The crowd gasped — he hadn’t spoken her name in weeks.
Together, they sang one last time, two hearts bound by melody and love.

After his passing, Gaga said softly:

“He saved me when I was lost.
I just hope I made him feel loved when he started to forget.” 💫

Some duets never end

title: Judy Garland - Tony Bennett - I Left My Heart In San Francisco
desc:
July 30, 1963:  Videotaping of "Episode Five" of "The Judy Garland Show" at CBS Television City, Stage 43, Hollywood.

Judy's guests for this episode were Tony Bennett and Dick Shawn.

Judy's songs: "If Love Were All" (cut before the broadcast but the footage still exists); "Yes, Indeed" (with Bennett and Shawn); "Garland-Bennett Medley" (including a duet on "I Left My Heart In San Francisco"); "My Buddy" (with Shawn); and in the "Born In A Trunk" segment: "Stormy Weather" preceded by her story about a moth flying into her mouth while on stage at the Greek Theater; and "I Will Come Back."
